description: The thesis's index sleeve: hold `symbol` while its 12-month return is positive (checked monthly), otherwise cash.
evidence: SPY 1994-2026: 10.6%/yr vs 10.8% buy & hold, worst drop -34% vs -55%; robust across periods, markets and costs. Cost ~1%/yr in 2014-2026 (fast rebounds).

status: tested, no edge over SPY sleeve
description: Index rotation ("dual momentum"): each month, rank major index funds by momentum (12-month return, or a blend of lookbacks) and hold the best `top` - or, with drop_worst=N, everything except the N weakest. Only funds with positive momentum are held; a failing slot sits in cash (earning T-bills). weighting: equal slices, or "rank" (the leader gets the biggest slice). With symbols=SPY and top=1 this is index_momentum.
evidence: 2004-2026, 6 indices (SPY QQQ IWM DIA EFA EEM): top 2 11.6%/yr, Sharpe 0.60 vs the SPY sleeve 9.4%, 0.58 - more risk, same Sharpe; gains all from 2004-12, relies on QQQ, fragile to lookback; walk-forward 8.3% (0.45) vs 10.2% (0.61). 'Avoid the worst' (drop_worst, rank weights): Sharpe 0.54-0.58, walk-forward 8.0% (0.44). No improvement inside the desk.
parameters: symbols=['SPY', 'QQQ', 'IWM', 'DIA', 'EFA', 'EEM']; top=1; lookback=252; drop_worst=0; weighting=equal; lookbacks=

description: Moving-average crossover on each symbol. Each gets an equal slice (1/N of the account) and holds it while its fast average is above its slow one; a symbol that's "off" leaves its slice in cash.
evidence: 50/200 on SPY: same insurance as momentum, near-identical results. Not in the live mix.
Duopoly pairs long/short: market-neutral but ~1%/yr above T-bills, cost-sensitive. Not in the live mix.
parameters: pairs=[('V', 'MA'), ('KO', 'PEP'), ('HD', 'LOW'), ('UPS', 'FDX'), ('MCO', 'SPGI'), ('BKNG', 'EXPE')]; lookback=60; entry_z=2.0; exit_z=0.5; max_days=60; mode=long_short

description: Top 25 of the quality stock screen, equal weight, re-picked every quarter (backtested: quarterly beat annual - research/screen_backtest.py). Positions drift between re-picks; no stop-loss (none was backtested).
evidence: Point-in-time 2014-2026: top 25 re-picked quarterly 17.9%/yr (Sharpe 0.89) vs same-universe 11.4% and SPY 13.8%; edge vs universe t~1.8. Survivors-only prices.
notes: Winners study (research/WINNERS.md): across 31 five-year windows, high ROIC / margins / FCF margin and low debt cut the chance of a bust by 20-40% but barely raised the chance of a top-decile winner (1.1-1.5x). Quality is a way to lose less, not to find 10-baggers. A walk-forward composite of all traits did not beat random (hit rate 6% vs 10%).

description: Top 8 of the bottleneck scan (python -m ai_desk bottleneck scan).
evidence: Only the price-flow part is testable: 100-day MA, re-picked every 2 weeks 17.0%/yr (Sharpe 0.60, -46% worst drop) vs SPY 13.7% (0.75); an isolated best setting. Fundamental fingerprints, insider signal and theme map untested.
notes: Winners study (research/WINNERS.md): the 2021-26 top 25 shared a theme (AI hardware and power), not a fundamental profile - median ROIC and margins sat below the universe's. Price momentum and growth showed no reliable edge across 31 windows. Case for this sleeve is following the theme and exiting when the trend breaks, not finding it early; the 100-day exit matters more than the entry.

description: Top 20 large companies by 6-month price gain (skipping the latest week), above their 200-day average, equal weight (python -m ai_desk momentum scan).
evidence: 2014-2026, top 20 of the 750 largest by 6-month return, re-picked every 4 weeks, with the 100-day exit: 19.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.76, worst drop -30% as a sleeve (vs the flow rotation's 17.8%, 0.63, -45%); desk 16.5%/yr, Sharpe 0.92 vs 0.88. Survivors-only prices.

status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
description: Michael Sikand's 'asymmetric bets' style (Autopilot pilot), as testable rules: a stock in a hot industry, fast revenue growth, cheaper than its industry peers on price-to-sales, 30-75% off its 12-month high; hold the top 5 at 20% each, re-picked monthly.
evidence: 2014-2026 on the 750 largest US companies: 0.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.00 vs the average stock 11.1% (0.59) and SPY 13.6% (0.81); every variant lost to the average stock. Buying 30-75% off the high cost 0.61%/month (52-week-high effect); only the industry-momentum rule helped. Survivors-only prices.
parameters: theme=industry in top quarter by 6-month momentum; growth=revenue growth top third, >15%; discount=P/S below industry median; off_high=30-75% below 12-month high; holdings=5; rebalance=monthly

status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
description: Swing trading on VCP breakouts (Minervini's volatility contraction pattern, from the vcp-screener skill in tradermonty/claude-trading-skills) as fixed rules: a stock in a strong uptrend, a quiet tightening pause, then a breakout above its 20-day high on 1.5x volume; bought at the next open.
evidence: 2014-2026: 2.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.13 vs the average stock 12.1% (0.59) and SPY 13.7% (0.72); 1,123 trades, 39% winners, +0.38% per trade; loses money at 0.30% costs; no setting tested gets above 5.6%/yr. Beats random strong-trend picks, so the pattern adds a little. Survivors-only prices.
parameters: positions=up to 10 of 10%; stop=8% below entry; exit=close below the 50-day average; target=+25%; max_hold=40 trading days; universe=750 largest US companies

status: tested, no edge (not in the live mix)
description: ICT (Inner Circle Trader) day-trading models as fixed rules on the 100 largest US companies: the Silver Bullet (5-min fair value gap after a liquidity sweep, 10-11am New York) and the Judas swing (fade a first-hour fake-out beyond the prior day's high/low), optionally with the quality score choosing the side (long strong companies, short weak ones) or a 50-day trend filter.
evidence: Silver Bullet (60 days, 2,974 trades): +0.01R before costs, -0.06% per trade after (t -3.5). Judas swing (3 years, 21,483 trades): -0.01R, -0.07% after costs (t -10), negative in all 13 quarters. Same as a coin-flip direction. Financial bias, long only, reaches break-even at best; trend filter worse.
parameters: target=2R; stop=beyond the sweep; exit=end of day; costs=0.03% each way; universe=100 largest US companies

description: Account-level circuit breaker (drawdown-circuit-breaker skill, tradermonty/claude-trading-skills): after a 2% day, 5% week or 8% month, no new buys (or: go to cash) until the next day / Monday / month.
evidence: On the desk 2014-2026 (daily): no breaker 16.4%/yr, Sharpe 0.81, worst -33.4%; freeze 15.9%, 0.79, -33.4%; go to cash 11.1%, 0.61, -35.7%. The desk buys only at re-picks, so freezing rarely matters, and cutting to cash misses the rebounds. Survivors-only prices.
parameters: day_limit=0.02; week_limit=0.05; month_limit=0.08; modes=freeze buys | go to cash
